rows.body: General considerations for an INR-based family office, drawn from public market data in this read. They do not reflect the family's holdings, goals, liquidity needs or tax position, and they are not investment advice. Discuss any change with your advisers.

rows.title: Rupee and global allocation
rows.body: The rupee weakened 7.0% against the dollar over 12 months, which lifted the rupee value of every dollar asset, but it strengthened 0.9% in October and USD/INR stands at ₹92.79, against 95.83 at the end of September.
rows.note: For an INR-based family, currency is often the biggest single driver of global returns. A stronger rupee trims the rupee value of existing overseas holdings but makes new overseas investment cheaper. Hedging dollar exposure back to rupees costs roughly the gap between Indian and US interest rates, so it is not free.

rows.title: Indian rates and fixed income
rows.body: The RBI raised the repo rate to 5.50% in October with retail inflation at 6.09%, above its 6% ceiling. The 10-year G-Sec yield rose 0.32pp to 7.38% and the 10-year G-Sec index lost 1.1% in the month. Markets price an 88% chance of another 25bp hike on 4 December, though that market is thin.
rows.note: While the RBI is still hiking, longer-duration bonds and debt funds lose value as yields rise; once the cycle peaks, the same higher yields become an opportunity to lock in income. Since April 2023 most debt-fund gains are taxed at the slab rate, which changes how bonds compare with other income options.

rows.title: Indian equities
rows.body: Foreign investors sold a net ₹34,843 crore of Indian equities in October, a second month of selling, yet the Nifty 50 rose 2.0% because domestic buyers absorbed it. Mid caps fell 3.7% and small caps 5.8%. Options price a Nifty move of about ±3.5% by the 29 December expiry.
rows.note: The market is leaning on domestic flows such as SIPs, insurers and mutual funds. That has been resilient, but if foreign selling continues while rates rise, mid and small caps, which are more rate-sensitive and less liquid, tend to feel it first.

rows.title: Oil and inflation
rows.body: Iran-war fears drove Brent up 17.7% in rupees in October and past $110 mid-month; it has since fallen to $92.3. Indian energy stocks fell 4.6% even as oil rallied.
rows.note: India imports most of its oil, so crude feeds inflation, the trade deficit and the rupee, and it shapes how far the RBI has to go. Oil has eased in November, which helps, but the Middle East remains an active risk.

rows.title: Global tech and AI
rows.body: Semiconductors fell 15.0% in rupees while Nifty IT rose 18.1%. Leveraged funds are the most bullish on Nasdaq 100 futures in three years (94th percentile) even though the index fell 6.7%, and markets put a 36% chance on an AI bubble bursting by June 2027.
rows.note: Many global portfolios are concentrated in US mega-cap tech without meaning to be. Crowded bullish positioning in a falling market can turn a correction into a sharper fall. Indian IT services are a different, less crowded way into the same AI theme.

rows.title: Gold and silver
rows.body: Gold fell 7.4% and silver 18.9% in rupees in October as rate expectations rose; markets put 62% odds on gold falling to $3,500 by December. Indian gold ran 2.22pp ahead of international gold last month because of the local premium.
rows.note: Gold's job in an Indian portfolio is usually a hedge against rupee weakness and crises, not a return driver. Rising real rates are its main headwind. Indian gold can drift several points away from international gold in a month, so where it is held matters.

rows.title: US rates and the Fed
rows.body: Markets price a 94% chance of a 25bp Fed hike on 9 December and no cuts this year. US long Treasuries still rose 5.6% in dollars in October on safe-haven buying, while asset managers hold their smallest Treasury bond long in three years (0th percentile).
rows.note: Another Fed hike tends to lift the dollar, pressure emerging markets including India, and hurt long-duration US bonds. With bond positioning already light, a turn in sentiment could move Treasuries sharply either way.

rows.title: Check risk against a Mixed regime
rows.body: If allocations were set for the risk-on backdrop of September, consider rebalancing to policy weights rather than adding risk while credit spreads widen and defensive sectors lead.
rows.note: When the regime gauge returns to risk-on, or the US high-yield spread passes 4%.

rows.title: Use the stronger rupee for planned overseas investment
rows.body: With USD/INR at ₹92.79 against 95.83 at the end of September, consider whether planned overseas remittances under the LRS limit should go ahead now rather than wait, and whether any part of the dollar exposure is worth hedging given the cost.
rows.note: If USD/INR moves above 96 or below 91.

rows.title: Keep Indian bond duration short until the RBI cycle turns
rows.body: While inflation is above 6% and further hikes are priced, consider favouring shorter-duration or floating-rate debt, and plan to extend duration once the RBI signals a peak.
rows.note: After the 4 December decision, and when the 10-year yield passes 7.5%.

rows.title: Test Indian equity holdings for rate and flow sensitivity
rows.body: Consider how much of the Indian equity allocation sits in mid and small caps that depend on continued domestic inflows, and whether the mix still fits if foreign selling persists.
rows.note: If foreign selling reaches three months running.

rows.title: Look through to US tech and semiconductor concentration
rows.body: Consider how much of the global allocation is effectively US mega-cap tech and semiconductors across all funds, given crowded bullish positioning in a falling market.
rows.note: If the VIX rises above 30 or the AI-bubble odds keep climbing.

rows.title: Decide how gold is held
rows.body: Consider whether gold exposure should sit in Indian instruments or international ones, given the local premium can swing several points in a month.
rows.note: If the Indian premium moves by more than 3pp in a month.

rows.title: Plan around the 4–9 December decisions
rows.body: With the RBI on 4 December and the Fed on 9 December, consider agreeing rebalancing bands in advance so that any decisions are not made on the day of a surprise.
